target_customer: Mobile app developers and publishers selling in-app subscriptions on iOS and Android
problem: Building and maintaining server infrastructure to validate and manage Apple and Google in-app subscriptions was hard and error-prone for app teams.
business_model: SaaS with revenue-based pricing on tracked revenue above a free threshold

founders.name: Jacob Eiting
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (July 23, 2018) says he was CTO of Elevate; the company's Series A post says he built the SDKs.

founders.name: Miguel Carranza
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is a software engineer from Seville who moved to Silicon Valley to work at Elevate; TechCrunch says director of engineering there. The Series A post says he built the backend.

technical_complexity.rationale: Receipt validation, cross-store entitlements, webhooks and SDKs for two platforms are standard engineering with many edge cases around Apple and Google billing behavior.

defensibility.rationale: Once embedded in an app's purchase flow it is costly to rip out, and aggregate data across apps adds insight, but the core idea can be rebuilt by a funded team.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platforms did not replace it. The company reportedly rejected a roughly $500M acquisition offer at the end of 2024 (OnlyCFO) and raised a Series C extension in 2025.

market_need_then: The founders had experienced the pain at Elevate, whose shift to recurring subscriptions saved that company per TechCrunch. The Series B article says that when they started in 2017 no one else was building similar tools.

branding.domain_note: Company site is revenuecat.com. Backup servers use the playful domain 8-lives-cat.io.

identity.mascot_or_character: Cat theme; employees' cats are called RevenueKitties on the company blog
identity.voice_and_tone: Casual and playful, for example the blog post Meet the Cats of RevenueCat

branding.brand_signature: The cat motif, including the 8-lives-cat.io failover domain
branding.community_and_virality: Company blog features staff cats and a press kit under revenuecat.com/cat; no merch or community metrics were found.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear, ownable cat motif and a name that states the value, with developer-friendly voice. Evidence of external virality was not found.

outcome_analysis: RevenueCat started with tens of customers and under $1,000 MRR at the seed in 2018 and reached about 157 apps by end of 2018. Founders who had lived the subscription problem at Elevate built developer-friendly SDKs, then raised Series A in 2020, B at $300M in 2021 and a C extension at about $500M in 2025 while reportedly rejecting a roughly $500M acquisition. Growth came from a developer-led, usage-priced product inside the subscription app boom.
notes: Competitors left empty: the TechCrunch 2018 article, Series A post and Series B article name none, and the Series B article says no one else built similar tools in 2017. The seed investors beyond Jason Lemkin are not named in the Series A post. The 2024 Series C and the 2025 Series C extension amounts and investors come from search result summaries (TechCrunch, Business Wire, Pulse 2.0 and Crowdfund Insider); the pages were not opened. Total raised conflicts across trackers ($68.5M to $119M); the figure of $100M after the 2025 round is the most cited. SaaStr retrospective reports a $60M valuation at Series A, not confirmed in an opened source. The Series B article was fetched through a TechCrunch shortlink.
